column1: # Which op families convert their activations once, at the start of the op, to the model's precision, per card.
# Tensors between ops stay f32. The copy is a scratch buffer owned by this folder.
# How the rows are used: act-copy/gen-act-copy.cmake compiles them in when CMake configures (act-copy-table.h), and
# ggml_metal_act_copy_decide_in (act-copy/decide.cpp) picks the row of the op's family, route and card. No file is read at run time.
# To change a row: run its test on that card first, then set applies. A new family first needs a kernel entry that reads the copy's type.
#   family: the op family, as named in lanes/lanes.tsv (matmul | flash-attn).
#   route: the route of that family whose kernel reads the copy, as named in lanes/lanes.tsv (for example mm-tiled).
#   pci: the card as 0xVVVV:0xDDDD (PCI vendor and device id, lower-case hex). A card with no row for a family and route gets no copy.
#   copy: the type the activations are converted to: bf16 | f16. It applies only when it equals the model's precision.
#   applies: yes | no. no = the row is documented but the op reads its f32 activations as before.
#   min_rereads: the op must read each activation at least this many times, else no copy. A number from 4 (below 4 the conversion never pays).
#   max_bytes: the largest copy taken, in bytes. A larger activation is read as f32.
#   reason: why the row has its applies value (what was measured, or that nothing was). Free text, no tab.
#   test: the command that proves the row on the card before applies is set to yes. Free text, no tab.
